# DSR-1.8 handler ownership and token enforcement

Status: Research complete, with implementation and gateway API decisions open.

Date: 2026-09-30. This note addresses DSR-1.8 only. It does not implement the base class, interceptor, token verification or changes to G3. No paid model run or Temporal server test was performed.

## Evidence versions

- The approved local source checkout reports HEAD `69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379`. Fork links below use that immutable revision.
- The plugin requires `temporalio>=1.33.0,<2` in [pyproject.toml, lines 18-23](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/pyproject.toml#L18-L23). Its [lockfile, lines 1269-1272](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/uv.lock#L1269-L1272) selects 1.33.0.
- Atlas was queried before SDK source reads. The Atlas SDK checkout reports revision `35b24bb28edf40fc3e2d3c446ea77a0cba312f6f`; it is supplementary evidence, not evidence of the locked dependency. Reads used `scripts/atlas/read.sh` exclusively.
- GitHub's tag API resolves SDK 1.33.0 to commit `ab52fdde33ee8ed193402625bfdba25d240a762d`. The override check and interceptor dispatch below were read again at this exact commit through the GitHub API.
- The live Temporal Docs connector was discovered through the runtime tool catalog and called successfully. Its current references support the public concepts; exact 1.33.0 source controls compatibility claims in this note.

## Current fork ownership

Problem: `DurableClaudeAgent` is a helper, not a decorated Workflow class. Its `validate_decision`, `decide`, `pending_approvals` and `state` methods do not register public handlers. The Workflow author declares the handlers and chooses public names. Source: [helper methods, lines 342-418](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/src/temporalio/claude_agent_sdk/_workflow.py#L342-L418).

| Current declaration | Public name | Owner and behavior | Immutable source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Update | `review` | Refund example Workflow calls `agent.decide`; name and signature belong to the Workflow. | [refund/workflows.py, lines 82-86](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/tests/refund/workflows.py#L82-L86) |
| Update validator | `check_review`, attached to `review` | Workflow calls `agent.validate_decision`; validator function name is not a separate client endpoint. | [refund/workflows.py, lines 88-92](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/tests/refund/workflows.py#L88-L92) |
| Queries | `pending_approvals`, `tool_calls`, `cost_usd` | Refund example Workflow exposes helper state. | [refund/workflows.py, lines 94-107](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/tests/refund/workflows.py#L94-L107) |
| Update and validator | `review`, with `check_review` | Endless example Workflow supplies reviewer identity and delegates to the same helper. | [endless/workflows.py, lines 86-95](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/tests/endless/workflows.py#L86-L95) |
| Signal | `review_by_signal` | Endless example Workflow calls `agent.decide` through an unsigned Signal. | [endless/workflows.py, lines 97-100](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/tests/endless/workflows.py#L97-L100) |
| Queries | `pending_approvals`, `progress` | Endless approval Workflow exposes waiting calls and totals. | [endless/workflows.py, lines 102-110](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/tests/endless/workflows.py#L102-L110) |
| Query | `runs` | Two lifecycle example Workflow classes expose the helper run count. | [lifecycle/workflows.py, lines 73-76](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/tests/lifecycle/workflows.py#L73-L76), [lines 143-146](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/tests/lifecycle/workflows.py#L143-L146) |
| Other message handlers | Update `ask`, Signal `ask`, Signal `send` | Other examples control tasks or chat messages; these are not signed human decision endpoints. | [lifecycle/workflows.py, lines 67-76](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/tests/lifecycle/workflows.py#L67-L76), [lines 116-119](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/tests/lifecycle/workflows.py#L116-L119), [endless/workflows.py, lines 159-167](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/tests/endless/workflows.py#L159-L167) |

The helper checks that the tool call is waiting, that it has no decision and that a supplied approver name appears in the configured list. It does not verify a signed token. `decide` catches those validation failures, logs and returns false. This behavior does not authenticate the supplied name.

The current state carry contains session, checkpoint, pending tool results, recent call ids, counters, cost, run count, fork flag and stream state. It does not contain the proposed `pending_decisions`, signed decision ids, key set or park state. `pending` means tool results awaiting delivery, not human decisions. Sources: [AgentState, lines 114-151](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/src/temporalio/claude_agent_sdk/_models.py#L114-L151), [state copy, lines 397-418](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/src/temporalio/claude_agent_sdk/_workflow.py#L397-L418).

## Two relayed claims checked at source

- **Verified at source:** fork handover passes no `initial_versioning_behavior`. Its actual call is `workflow.continue_as_new(args=self._new_run_args(state))`. Before it, handover drains handlers, increments the run counter and carries the stream. [Fork `_workflow.py`, lines 458-476](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/src/temporalio/claude_agent_sdk/_workflow.py#L458-L476). This proves omission, not which version the server routes the next run to. No rollout was tested.
- **Verified with a precision correction:** SDK definition validation does not inspect an overridden handler body or enforce token checks. It also performs structural checks beyond decorators, including Update/validator parameter agreement. Base traversal checks whether inherited registered names remain present; it is not an authorization mechanism. [SDK 1.33.0 `_definition.py`, lines 342-397](https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-python/blob/ab52fdde33ee8ed193402625bfdba25d240a762d/temporalio/workflow/_definition.py#L342-L397). The phrase “only checks that the override repeats the decorator” is an imprecise summary, especially for Updates: the surrounding base traversal first filters for ordinary functions. No claim that inheritance blocks every form of Update override is justified.

## Proposed ownership and public API

Solution proposal: the plugin owns one Workflow base class and one inbound interceptor implementation. The application's registered concrete Workflow owns its run method and explicit `@workflow.defn` versioning configuration. Registration must verify the protected handler set, validators, interceptor installation and Pinned configuration. A base class alone does not supply an enforced Pinned default: the SDK's `defn` documentation says the decorator must be on the registered class and is ignored on a base class ([SDK definition, lines 60-75](https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-python/blob/ab52fdde33ee8ed193402625bfdba25d240a762d/temporalio/workflow/_definition.py#L60-L75)).

Client names for gateway review in DSR-0.7: Updates `decide`, `answer_question`, `resume`; Queries `pending_decisions`, `last_effect_outcomes`, `parked_state`. The plan's Architecture table already names `answer_question`; this note preserves that name. Query spellings remain proposed because the specification describes their results without fixing every endpoint spelling. The base declares each Update and its validator, using a token envelope. It declares no answer Signal and no unsigned decision Signal in policy mode. Registration and gateway compatibility remain unimplemented.

Single proposed token enforcement authority: a plugin owned deterministic verification function invoked by the inbound interceptor before forwarding a protected message. Base handlers record the validated decision and enforce state rules; they do not become an alternate independent authorization path. Legacy behavior remains a separate configuration when `tool_policy` is `None`.

Two limits must be addressed by DSR-3.2:

- An interceptor matching only Signal name `decide` misses the fork's actual `review_by_signal`. Arbitrary custom Signal or Update names could also call the helper. Policy registration must exclude unapproved decision aliases and dynamic paths, or explicitly enumerate and protect them. Neither a base class nor a name match prevents arbitrary application code from changing state.
- The SDK calls `handle_update_validator` only when `job.run_validator` is true **and** a validator exists. Removing a validator can bypass an interceptor implemented only at that stage. Registration must require validators for protected Updates; handler interception needs a compatible deterministic check as well. [SDK 1.33.0 dispatch, lines 706-725](https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-python/blob/ab52fdde33ee8ed193402625bfdba25d240a762d/temporalio/worker/_workflow_instance.py#L706-L725). The handler stage is after acceptance, so it cannot replace rejection before history.

## Proposed G3 wording

“G3 applies only to Workflows built on the plugin's validated Workflow base and registered with its token enforcement interceptor and required validators. Those Workflows preserve pending human decisions across the supported handover path and accept them only through the protected signed decision API. A Workflow that omits that registration or exposes another decision path has no G3 guarantee.”

This is proposed wording. The fork does not provide this guarantee today. DSR-3.2 and the handover tests must prove it before it is published as implemented behavior.

## Replay and patching

Verified source fact: the SDK constructs the inbound interceptor chain as part of each Workflow instance. Signal and Update handler dispatch run through that chain. [SDK 1.33.0 instance construction, lines 424-435](https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-python/blob/ab52fdde33ee8ed193402625bfdba25d240a762d/temporalio/worker/_workflow_instance.py#L424-L435), [Signal dispatch, lines 2680-2687](https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-python/blob/ab52fdde33ee8ed193402625bfdba25d240a762d/temporalio/worker/_workflow_instance.py#L2680-L2687), and the Update dispatch cited above. Validators are conditional; accepted Update handlers still reconstruct their state on replay. Current [Temporal message passing documentation](https://docs.temporal.io/develop/python/workflows/message-passing#updates) describes rejection in validators before acceptance is recorded.

Inference: Signal interception and Update handler verification are replay relevant Workflow code. Adding strict token requirements to existing unsigned histories can suppress previously accepted decisions or raise during reconstruction. Verification must use deterministic canonicalization, immutable run input keys, Workflow time and the same historical decisions on replay. Never use wall clock time, network key lookup or a current process key set there. Do not apply expiry to a historically accepted Update at a later live clock time.

Patching answer: a fresh workflow type with no old histories needs no compatibility patch for its initial token enforcement. An existing workflow type with unsigned histories needs a compatible route, such as retaining its old Worker version until completion or an explicit tested patch for code that changes replay behavior. Blanket use of `workflow.patched` inside a validator is not an established solution because validation is read only and is not replayed on every accepted Update. Owner: Plugin engineer in DSR-3.2 must choose the migration route and prove it with an old unsigned history, a signed history and invalid direct frontend Updates. No patch or crypto sandbox test was run for this note.

## Acceptance results

| DSR-1.8 criterion | Result | Evidence or residual |
|---|---|---|
| Current handler, validator and Query names with pinned fork links | PASS | Current ownership table and state carry above. |
| Ownership split and one token enforcement point | PASS as a research proposal | Proposed base, registration and interceptor responsibilities above. Gateway endpoint compatibility remains DSR-0.7. |
| Two relayed statements checked at source | PASS | Handover omission verified; override statement verified with precision correction at locked SDK revision. |
| Guarantee limit without base class | PASS as proposed wording | Proposed G3 sentence above; no implementation claim. |
| Replay implications and patch question | PASS | Source facts and conditional patch answer above; migration and replay proof remain DSR-3.2. |

The M1 research part of A-15 has evidence. The M3 enforcement, sandbox and forged frontend Update proof remain open. This note does not retire the whole assumption.
